title: MMS LITE
author: Brandon Lessard
desc: Full body mass building program for novice and intermediate lifters.

ex.note: Strive for 3 x 5 with your manageable dumbbell. Keep the rest periods short.
Add weight to each set. Over the weeks, strive for bodyweight on the last set here.
Really trying to hold the squeeze in the finished position. Go as heavy as you can get five reps in.
How many sets does it take you to get to 25 reps?
The last set should still keep a couple of reps in the tank.
Keep your eye on slowly increasing the weight on the bar here. Although adding reps is tempting (“I feel the pump!”), mass gaining is all about load.
One set with heavy dumbbells. Try to make your walk end in front of the racks. You will thank me later.
Strive for 5 x 5 with your manageable dumbbell. Keep the rest periods short.
Add weight to the second set. This is a set up workout for Workout C.
Really trying to hold the squeeze in the finished position. Go just a little lighter than in Workout A.
How many sets does it take you to get to 15 reps?
Warm up with a few easy reps before you start counting the sets. All five sets should be relatively heavy.
It’s okay to feel the burn and pump today.
Two sets today. Walk out as far as you can from the rack and put the weights down. Then, simply return them!
Strive for 3 x 5 with your manageable dumbbell. Keep the rest periods short.
Add weight to each set. Plan the workout so that set four is bodyweight and set five is just a bit more. This last set is the one that makes or breaks your training.

How many sets does it take you to get to 12 reps?
The last set should still keep a couple of reps in the tank. Rein it in a little today.
The best of both worlds in the curl today: a little strength and then finish off with getting some blood in the biceps.
